question: Is the PTRACE reference itself double-run deterministic at every ladder rung? Any rung where it diverges from itself is disqualified as a golden.

first.method: N=5 independent pairs per rung, INFO log, timestamp-stripped byte compare. Stopped at the first divergence.
first.result: 0 divergences in 55 pairs; disqualification list reported EMPTY.

deep.method: N=300 independent pairs per rung (11 rungs), plus a 3800-pair controlled matrix varying env (inherited vs --base-env minimal) and cwd (busy vs quiescent), each pair scored under three comparators. Does NOT stop at first divergence, so a flaky rung yields a rate rather than an existence claim.
deep.result: 9 divergent pairs in 7100. Disqualification list is NOT empty: 2 Set-A rung configurations flake. All 7 pinned goldens qualify (0/2100).

comparison_depth: INFO log (Detcore COMMIT + DETLOG records), NOT stdout-only. Plus a separate DEBUG-depth class analysis.

comparators.WHOLE: whole timestamp-stripped log; what the golden uses today
comparators.STREAM: DETLOG + COMMIT lines only; immune to startup-banner reordering, NOT to ambient host state
comparators.COMMIT: COMMIT turns only; immune to everything observed, but discards the syscall detail a golden exists to carry -- NOT recommended

A-ratchet-f89c69766.provenance: baked-in SHA, no -dirty suffix (contrast: the primary checkout's binary reports gf89c69766371-dirty)
A-ratchet-f89c69766.why: the SHA the prefix-depth ratchet captured its golden at

disqualified_rungs.cause: guest stats a live directory; the directory's st_size is written into DETLOG. Observed deltas 1662->1692, 1622->1644, 1692->1698, /home/newton 6032->5924, . 106->132. Ambient host filesystem state, mutated by 18 agents sharing the box and (for the '.' case) by this experiment's own file writes.
disqualified_rungs.eliminated_by: --base-env minimal -> 0 divergent in 400 pairs, same guest argv, same cwd, same time window

disqualified_rungs.config: Set A, FULL INHERITED ENV, 11-way concurrency
disqualified_rungs.rate: 1 divergent in 300 pairs under 11-way concurrency; 0 in 1500 pairs under 4-way
disqualified_rungs.cause: startup log-interleaving race: the scheduler daemon's banner races the root thread's SCHEDRAND/USERRAND/CHAOSRAND seeding lines. The two logs are IDENTICAL AS MULTISETS (489 lines each) and the 52-COMMIT stream is byte-identical. Pure emission-order difference.
disqualified_rungs.eliminated_by: not eliminated; load-dependent. STREAM comparator is immune to it.

invariant_that_never_broke: In all 7100 INFO-depth pairs, across every rung, both SHAs, both envs and both cwd conditions, the COMMIT stream was BYTE-IDENTICAL. Zero exceptions. No observed divergence was hermit scheduling nondeterminism.

classes: 1. wall clock: 'Nondeterministic realtime elapsed' -- hermit self-labels this; benign
2. host CPU identity: initial_local_apic_id, x2apic_id, core_id, max_cores_for_cache -- which core/CCX the host scheduler picked
3. hex addresses: host-side vdso patch targets -- host ASLR
4. DECIMAL addresses: inject SyscallArgs { arg1: 94011568533984 } -- the same ASLR, decimal-rendered; a hex-keyed canonicalizer misses these
5. vdso patch ORDER: symbols patched in a permuted sequence -- iteration over a randomly-seeded Rust hash container. NOT an address problem; no address canonicalizer can remove it.
debug_depth.correction_to_first_pass: The first pass named only classes 1 and 4 and recommended fixing decimal-address canonicalization before deepening past INFO. That is necessary but NOT sufficient: classes 2, 3 and especially 5 remain. Class 5 must also be canonicalized BEFORE address ordinals are assigned, since the permutation changes the order addresses are first seen and ordinal-mapping first can never converge.
debug_depth.guest_side_is_clean: The guest-side vdso address (@7ffff7fc2fe0) is identical across runs while the host-side one is not; the guest address space is properly determinized.

statistical_strength.first_pass_per_rung: 0/5 -> ~45% one-sided 95% upper bound on a per-pair flake rate
statistical_strength.caveat: Still an upper bound, not a proof. 0/300 means 'not observed to diverge in 300 pairs'.

not_established: The load curve of the startup logger race. Observed 1/300 at 11-way concurrency and 0/1500 at 4-way; no single rate is quotable and I did not characterize the dependence.

Set A's Z counts (23/52/53/182) differ from the ratchet doc's (14/43/44/16) because the ratchet's env and exact fork/exec guest are not recorded in that doc; Set A rungs APPROXIMATE its ladder rather than reproduce it. 'Disqualified' therefore binds to the rungs as run here.

Set B used a debug build at the golden SHA, not the manifest's exact release binary (sha256 differs). The Z counts (5,6,7,7,7,30,45) match the pinned manifest exactly, which is the strongest available cross-check.
Whether the ambient-filesystem-state failure also affects rungs beyond fork-pipeline. Any guest that stats a mutable directory is exposed; only the rungs listed here were tested.
Whether the vdso patch-order nondeterminism (DEBUG class 5) can affect anything observable. It did not affect INFO or the COMMIT stream in any pair here.
